structured.reason: The description contains hedged performance language, which the criterion treats as a negative signal. "The brightly colored design makes brushing feel more like play, which can help make it a routine rather than a chore" uses the hedge "can help" and implies a contrast with a chore. Two further phrases are weaker but still count under the strict reading: "Give your child a toothbrush they will actually want to use" implies that other brushes fall short, and "The U-shaped head fits the contours of a child's mouth and is sized for ages 6 to 12" responds to the reviewer complaint that the brush was "a little too big" for a 6-year-old's mouth, so it addresses that complaint defensively. Because the criterion says to lean toward failing when unsure, the description fails.
